newsitem.title: USA: Bayoil wins U.N. appeal to load cancelled cargo.
newsitem.headline: Bayoil wins U.N. appeal to load cancelled cargo.

text.p: U.S. oil trader Bayoil won approval from the United Nations Wednesday to proceed with loading 1.3 million barrels of Iraqi Basrah Light crude, despite Iraqi attempts to cancel the deal, informed sources said.

Bayoil appealed to the overseers of the U.N. "oil-for-food" accord after Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) cancelled its 1.3 million-barrel cargo of Basrah Light crude oil at the last minute.
SOMO also cancelled a 900,000-barrel cargo for Nippon Oil, which the Japanese company accepted.

SOMO cancelled the cargoes even though they were given the green light by U.N. overseers last Friday, apparently because the U.N. said the cargoes could load but the receipts from its sale would be frozen until it was determined whether they would overshoot the $2.14 billion limit on the deal or until a renewal of the deal can be agreed.
Sources close to the deal said it was not yet clear if Bayoil would be allowed to load the entire 1.3 million barrels.
The source said Bayoil appealled on the grounds that it has a ship already waiting to load the crude.

"The money from the oil sales will be frozen," said the trader source. If Iraq's oil accord with the U.N. is extended, the Bayoil proceeds will be unfrozen and set against the next oil sales receipt limit, the source said.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to submit his recommendation on renewing the deal at the beginning of next week. Once the report is issued to the Security Council its 15 members must decide whether to renew and on what terms.
Iraq's current deal expires on June 7.

Baghad is allowed to sell $2.14 billion of oil from December 10 to June 7, with the proceeds mainly to buy food and medicine for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed after the invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
